claims.text: Enhancing chemical short-range order in multi-component concentrated alloys increases yield strength.
Chemical short-range order increases strength by impeding dislocation motion.
Processing that promotes chemical short-range order produces altered deformation behavior relative to an as-cast state.
The proposed as-cast baseline is a nominally random solid solution.
A controlled annealing treatment can promote chemical short-range order without significant grain growth or phase separation.
Chemical short-range order consists of spatial correlations among atomic species.
Chemical short-range order creates local compositional fluctuations that obstruct dislocation glide.
Increased chemical short-range order creates local regions of higher lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion and compositional fluctuations hinder dislocation nucleation.
Local lattice distortion and compositional fluctuations hinder dislocation glide.
Hindering dislocation nucleation and glide increases yield strength.
Chemical short-range order may alter strain localization and thereby affect deformation or failure behavior.
An annealed sample with enhanced chemical short-range order will have higher yield strength than the as-cast baseline.
Enhanced chemical short-range order may delay the onset of plasticity.
The hypothesis is expected to apply when significant grain growth and phase separation are avoided and testing is performed under similar room-temperature conditions.
The magnitude of the yield-strength increase depends on the degree of chemical short-range order produced by annealing.
Grain size must be controlled to isolate the effect of chemical short-range order.
A verified increase in chemical short-range order without a statistically significant increase in yield strength or altered deformation behavior would falsify the proposed mechanism.
